chapters.title: Coming Back In
chapters.html:
Leviticus 14

Outside the Camp, and the Two Birds

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"This shall be the instruction for the person with the blight on the day of his cleansing. He shall be brought to the priest,

3and the priest shall go outside the camp. The priest shall look. If the mark of blight has healed in the blighted man,

4the priest shall order that two live clean birds be taken for the one being cleansed, with cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop.

5The priest shall order that one of the birds be slaughtered into a clay pot, over fresh running water.

6He shall take the live bird with the cedar wood, the scarlet yarn and the hyssop, and dip them all in the blood of the bird slaughtered over the fresh running water,

7and sprinkle it seven times on the one being cleansed from the blight, and declare him clean; and he shall let the live bird go free over the open field.

8The one being cleansed shall wash his clothes and shave off all his hair and bathe in water, and he is clean. After that he may enter the camp — but he shall stay outside his tent for seven days.

9On the seventh day he shall shave off all his hair — his head, his beard and his eyebrows, every hair. He shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he is clean.

The Eighth Day

10On the eighth day he shall take two male lambs without defect, and one ewe lamb a year old without defect, and three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and one log of oil.

11The priest who does the cleansing shall set the man being cleansed, and these things, before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

12The priest shall take one of the lambs and present it as a guilt offering, with the log of oil, and wave them before the LORD.

13He shall slaughter the lamb in the place where the sin offering and the burnt offering are slaughtered, in the holy place — because the guilt offering, like the sin offering, belongs to the priest. It is most holy.

14The priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one being cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

15The priest shall take some of the log of oil and pour it into his own left palm,

16and dip his right finger in the oil on his left palm and sprinkle some of it with his finger seven times before the LORD.

17From the oil left in his palm the priest shall put some on the lobe of the right ear of the one being cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot — on top of the blood of the guilt offering.

18He shall put what is left of the oil in his palm on the head of the one being cleansed, and the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD.

19The priest shall offer the sin offering and make atonement for the one being cleansed from his uncleanness, and after that he shall slaughter the burnt offering.

20The priest shall offer up the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar, and make atonement for him, and he is clean.

If He Cannot Afford It

21If he is poor and cannot afford so much, he shall take one lamb as a guilt offering to be waved, to make atonement for him, and one tenth of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and a log of oil,

22and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford — one shall be a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.

23On the eighth day he shall bring them for his cleansing to the priest, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the LORD.

24The priest shall take the lamb of the guilt offering and the log of oil, and wave them before the LORD.

25He shall slaughter the lamb of the guilt offering, and the priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one being cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

26The priest shall pour some of the oil into his own left palm,

27and with his right finger sprinkle some of the oil in his left palm seven times before the LORD.

28From the oil in his palm the priest shall put some on the lobe of the right ear of the one being cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot — on the place where the blood of the guilt offering was.

29He shall put what is left of the oil in his palm on the head of the one being cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD.

30He shall offer the turtledoves or the young pigeons, whichever he can afford —

31one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, with the grain offering. The priest shall make atonement for the one being cleansed, before the LORD.

32This is the instruction for the person who has a mark of blight, who cannot afford the full offering for his cleansing."

Blight in a House

33The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

34"When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as a holding, and I put a mark of blight in a house in the land you hold,

35the owner of the house shall come and tell the priest, 'Something like a mark has appeared in my house.'

36The priest shall order the house emptied before he goes in to look at the mark, so that nothing in the house becomes unclean. After that the priest shall go in to look at the house.

37He shall look at the mark. If the mark is in the walls of the house, in greenish or reddish hollows that look lower than the wall,

38the priest shall go out of the house to its doorway and shut it up for seven days.

39The priest shall come back on the seventh day and look. If the mark has spread in the walls of the house,

The priest shall take one of the lambs and present it as a guilt offering, with the log of oil, and wave them before the LORD.

and dip his right finger in the oil on his left palm and sprinkle some of it with his finger seven times before the LORD.

chapters.title: What the Body Gives Off
chapters.html:
Leviticus 15

A Man with a Discharge

1The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

2"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When any man has a discharge from his body, his discharge is unclean.

3This is how his discharge makes him unclean: whether his body runs with it or is stopped up by it, he is unclean.

4Every bed the man with the discharge lies on is unclean, and everything he sits on is unclean.

5Anyone who touches his bed shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

6Whoever sits on anything the man with the discharge sat on shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

7Whoever touches the body of the man with the discharge shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

8If the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

9Anything he rides on is unclean.

10Anyone who touches anything that was under him shall be unclean until evening; and whoever carries those things shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

11If the man with the discharge touches anyone without first rinsing his hands in water, that person shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

12A clay pot that the man with the discharge touches shall be broken, and every wooden vessel shall be rinsed in water.

13When the man with the discharge becomes clean of his discharge, he shall count seven days for his cleansing, and wash his clothes and bathe his body in fresh running water, and he is clean.

14On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and come before the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and give them to the priest.

15The priest shall offer them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and make atonement for him before the LORD for his discharge.

Emissions

16When a man has an emission of semen, he shall bathe his whole body in water, and be unclean until evening.

17Every garment and every hide with semen on it shall be washed in water, and be unclean until evening.

18When a man lies with a woman and has an emission of semen, they shall both bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

A Woman's Flow

19When a woman has a discharge, and the discharge in her body is blood, she shall be in her monthly separation seven days, and anyone who touches her shall be unclean until evening.

20Everything she lies on in her separation is unclean, and everything she sits on is unclean.

21Anyone who touches her bed shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

22Anyone who touches anything she sits on shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

23If anything is on her bed or on whatever she is sitting on, whoever touches it shall be unclean until evening.

24If a man lies with her and her separation comes on him, he shall be unclean seven days, and every bed he lies on shall be unclean.

A Flow Out of Season

25When a woman's flow of blood runs many days at a time that is not her monthly separation, or when it runs past her separation, all the days of her unclean flow she shall be as in the days of her separation. She is unclean.

26Every bed she lies on all the days of her flow shall be to her like the bed of her separation, and everything she sits on shall be unclean, like the uncleanness of her separation.

27Anyone who touches these things shall be unclean, and shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

28When she becomes clean of her flow, she shall count seven days for herself, and after that she is clean.

29On the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest, to the entrance of the tent of meeting.

30The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and make atonement for her before the LORD for her unclean flow.

Why This Matters

31You shall keep the sons of Israel separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die in their uncleanness by defiling My dwelling, which is among them."

32This is the instruction for the man with a discharge, and for the man who has an emission of semen and is unclean by it,

33and for the woman who is unwell in her separation, and for anyone with a discharge, male or female, and for a man who lies with an unclean woman.

Notes

  • v3 the hard verse — rar besaro et zovo o hechtim besaro mi-zovo. Rar is a word for running or slavering; hechtim is built on chatam, to seal up. So the sentence covers the condition whether the flow is running or blocked, which is medically sensible and grammatically strange, and neither verb occurs often enough to be pinned down.

  • uncleanness is not sin — the distinction the whole chapter depends on, and the one most likely to be misread. Nothing described here is a wrong. Nobody is blamed, nobody is punished, and two of the causes are ordinary marital relations (v18) and a woman's monthly cycle (v19). The remedy is water and sunset, and for a long flow seven days and two birds (vv13–15, 28–30). Tamei is a status, like being wet — it says where a person may go, not what kind of person they are — and the only reason it matters at all is given in v31.

  • v24 and 20:18 do not agree — here, a man who lies with a woman in her separation is unclean for seven days, the same as the bed he slept on. At 20:18 the same act ends with both of them cut off from among their people. Two penalties for one action, in one book, and neither passage mentions the other. It is the kind of seam the Torah leaves visible. 15:24 says her separation comes on him; 20:18 says both uncover her flow.

  • v25 the woman whose flow does not stop — a chronic condition, treated at length and with no stigma attached beyond the same rules that apply to everyone else in the chapter. This is the law the woman in the crowd at Mark 5:25 has been living under: the Greek says she was in a flow of blood twelve years, using the word the Greek Old Testament uses for zov. What she then does is reach through a crowd and take hold of a man's cloak (5:27) — and by vv21–27 here, touching is exactly what transmits. In Mark the transmission runs the other way.

  • v31 the reason, finally — thirty verses of beds and seats and washing, and then the point: so that they do not die in their uncleanness by defiling My dwelling, which is among them. The rules are not about hygiene and not about morality. They exist because of where God has chosen to live. Mishkani, My dwelling, is the word from Exodus 25:9, and the last two words of the verse are the whole problem — asher be-tokham, which is among them. Something holy has been set down in the middle of an ordinary camp full of bodies, and the rest follows from that.

chapters.title: Once a Year
chapters.html:
Leviticus 16

After the Death of the Two Sons

1The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron's two sons, when they came near before the LORD and died.

2The LORD said to Moses, "Tell Aaron your brother that he must not come at just any time into the holy place inside the veil, in front of the cover on the ark, or he will die — because I appear in the cloud over the cover.

3This is how Aaron shall enter the holy place: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

4He shall put on a holy linen tunic, and linen undergarments shall be on his body, and he shall tie a linen sash around him and wind a linen turban on his head. These are holy garments. He shall bathe his body in water and put them on.

5From the congregation of the sons of Israel he shall take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.

The Two Goats

6Aaron shall present his own bull for the sin offering and make atonement for himself and for his household.

7He shall take the two goats and set them before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

8Aaron shall cast lots over the two goats: one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel.

9Aaron shall present the goat on which the lot for the LORD fell, and offer it as a sin offering.

10The goat on which the lot for Azazel fell shall be set alive before the LORD, to make atonement over it, to send it away to Azazel into the wilderness.

Inside the Veil

11Aaron shall present his own bull for the sin offering and make atonement for himself and for his household; he shall slaughter his own bull for the sin offering.

12He shall take a fire pan full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense, and bring them inside the veil.

13He shall put the incense on the fire before the LORD, and the cloud of the incense shall hide the cover that is over the Testimony, so that he does not die.

14He shall take some of the blood of the bull and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the cover, on the east side; and he shall sprinkle some of the blood seven times with his finger in front of the cover.

15He shall slaughter the people's goat for the sin offering and bring its blood inside the veil, and do with its blood as he did with the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it on the cover and in front of the cover.

16He shall make atonement for the holy place because of the uncleanness of the sons of Israel and because of their rebellions, for all their sins. So he shall do for the tent of meeting, which dwells with them in the middle of their uncleanness.

17No one at all shall be in the tent of meeting when he goes in to make atonement in the holy place, until he comes out. He shall make atonement for himself and for his household and for the whole assembly of Israel.

18He shall go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it, and take some of the blood of the bull and some of the blood of the goat and put it on the horns of the altar all around.

19He shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it from the uncleanness of the sons of Israel and set it apart.

The Goat That Goes Away

20When he has finished making atonement for the holy place and the tent of meeting and the altar, he shall present the live goat.

21Aaron shall lean both his hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the guilt of the sons of Israel and all their rebellions, for all their sins, and put them on the head of the goat, and send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a man appointed for it.

22The goat shall carry on itself all their guilt to a land cut off; and he shall send the goat away in the wilderness.

23Aaron shall go into the tent of meeting and take off the linen garments he put on when he went into the holy place, and leave them there.

24He shall bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his garments, and come out and offer his burnt offering and the people's burnt offering, and make atonement for himself and for the people.

25He shall turn the fat of the sin offering into smoke on the altar.

26The one who sends the goat away to Azazel shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and after that he may enter the camp.

27The bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, shall be carried outside the camp, and their hides and their flesh and their dung shall be burned in the fire.

28The one who burns them shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and after that he may enter the camp.

Once a Year

29This shall be a lasting statute for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month, you shall afflict yourselves and do no work at all — neither the native nor the guest living among you —

30because on this day atonement shall be made for you, to cleanse you. You shall be clean before the LORD from all your sins.

31It is a sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall afflict yourselves. It is a lasting statute.

32The priest who is anointed and whose hand is filled to serve as priest in place of his father shall make the atonement, and he shall put on the linen garments, the holy garments,

33and make atonement for the most holy place, for the tent of meeting and for the altar; and he shall make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.

34This shall be a lasting statute for you, to make atonement for the sons of Israel for all their sins once a year." He did as the LORD commanded Moses.

Notes

  • v8 "Azazel" — la-azazel, and nobody knows what it means. The word occurs four times in the Hebrew Bible, all of them in this chapter, and nowhere else. Three readings have been argued for centuries: that it is a compound of ez, goat, and azal, to go away — the source of English scapegoat, coined by Tyndale; that it is an abstract noun meaning utter removal; or that it is a name. The grammar of this verse leans to the third, because of the parallel it sets up — one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel — where the matching term is a person. The text says no more than that, and neither can anyone else.

  • v16 "which dwells with them in the middle of their uncleanness" — this is what the last five chapters were building toward. The tent is not a clean place set apart from a dirty camp; it is a holy thing sitting in the middle of ordinary human mess, and 15:31 already said the risk that creates. The atonement in this chapter is made for the building (v16) before it is made for the people (vv17, 24), and after Aaron's own (vv6, 11). The sanctuary itself needs cleaning, and what has dirtied it is everyone living around it.

  • v21 "both his hands" — the written consonants say his hand, singular; the reading tradition says his hands. Leviticus has five such places, and the other one where Aaron's hand is at issue is 9:22, where he lifts it to bless the people. Both are his hands on or toward Israel, and in both the tradition reads two where the letters say one. Note also that everywhere else in Leviticus one hand is leaned on an animal's head (1:4, 4:4). This is the only sacrifice that takes both.

  • v29 "you shall afflict yourselves" — te'annu et nafshoteikhem, you shall afflict your souls, and nefesh is the throat and the appetite as much as the inner life. The Torah does not use the word fast here or anywhere in this chapter. What is commanded is a day of doing without, undefined, and the tradition that made it a fast had to read the definition out of this phrase. What the verse does say plainly is who it binds: the native and the foreigner living among them, in the same clause.

chapters.title: The Life Is in the Blood
chapters.html:
Leviticus 17

Nowhere Else to Kill It

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all the sons of Israel, and say to them: This is what the LORD has commanded:

3Any man of the house of Israel who slaughters an ox or a sheep or a goat in the camp, or who slaughters it outside the camp,

4and has not brought it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before the dwelling of the LORD — blood shall be counted against that man. He has shed blood, and that man shall be cut off from among his people.

5This is so that the sons of Israel will take the sacrifices they have been making out in the open field and bring them to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, to the priest, and offer them as peace offerings to the LORD.

6The priest shall dash the blood against the altar of the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and turn the fat into smoke as a soothing aroma to the LORD.

7They shall no longer offer their sacrifices to the goat-spirits to whom they have been giving themselves. This shall be a lasting statute for them through their generations.

8Say to them: Any man of the house of Israel, or of the guests living among them, who offers up a burnt offering or a sacrifice

9and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to the LORD — that man shall be cut off from his people.

The Life Is in the Blood

10Any man of the house of Israel, or of the guests living among them, who eats any blood — I will set My face against the person who eats the blood, and cut that person off from among his people.

11For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives; for it is the blood that makes atonement by the life.

12That is why I have said to the sons of Israel: None of you shall eat blood, and the guest living among you shall not eat blood.

13Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the guests living among them, who hunts and catches an animal or a bird that may be eaten shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth.

14For the life of all flesh — its blood is its life. I said to the sons of Israel: You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, because the life of all flesh is its blood. Anyone who eats it shall be cut off.

15Any person, native or guest, who eats an animal that died on its own or was torn by beasts shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening, and then he is clean.

16But if he does not wash them and does not bathe his body, he carries his guilt."

Notes

  • vv3–9 the point of the restriction — an Israelite may not kill an ox anywhere but at the one door. Not because slaughter is wrong, but because sacrifice in the open field is what they have been doing, and to whom. The law does not argue with the practice; it moves it. Everything gets brought to one place where a priest can see it.

  • v4 "He has shed blood" — dam shafakh, and it is the language of murder. Genesis 9:6: one who sheds the blood of the human, by the human his blood shall be shed — the same verb with the same noun. A man who butchers his own ox in the wrong place is described in the vocabulary reserved for killing a person. The verb before it is yechashev, shall be counted, the accounting word from 7:18 and from Genesis 15:6: something is entered against his name.

  • v7 "the goat-spirits" — se'irim, hairy ones, the ordinary Hebrew word for he-goats, here plural with the article and clearly meaning something that can be sacrificed to. And it is the same word, in the same form, as the two goats of the previous chapter (16:8). One chapter after the Day of Atonement assigns two se'irim by lot, the next forbids sacrificing to the se'irim. Whatever they are — the word is used again of the creatures that dance in Babylon's ruins at Isaiah 13:21 — the text will not say more about them than that Israel has been going to them.

  • v7 "giving themselves to" — zonim achareihem, whoring after, from zanah, the plain word for prostitution. It is the Bible's standing picture for worshipping anything else, and it is not a polite one: the relationship is a marriage, and the offense is infidelity, not error.

  • vv8, 10, 12, 13, 15 "the guest" — ger, and the chapter names him in every single paragraph, five times in sixteen verses. The blood law is one of the few in Leviticus that binds the non-Israelite exactly as it binds the native. What is at stake here is not identity; it is the ground everyone is standing on.

  • v10 "I will set My face against" — ve-natatti panai, and God stops speaking through a procedure and speaks in the first person about an individual. Here, at 20:3, 5 and 6, and at 23:30 the sentence names Him; most other places say he shall be cut off, passive, with nobody named as doing the cutting. Here the sentence names Him twice over: I will set My face, and I will cut that person off.

  • v11 "the life of the flesh is in the blood" — nefesh ha-basar ba-dam hi, and nefesh is the word English Bibles usually print as soul. It is breath, throat, appetite, the living of a living thing — the word used of animals in Genesis 1 before it is ever used of a person. So this sentence is not metaphysics. It is a statement about what blood is: the life itself, in liquid form, which is why it may not be eaten and why it is the one substance that can be put on the altar in place of a life.

  • v11 "makes atonement by the life" — ba-nefesh yekhapper, two words that can be read at least three ways: the blood atones by means of the life in it, or in place of a life, or at the cost of a life. The preposition be carries all three and the verse does not choose. Its last clause has never been settled.

  • v13 covering the blood of a hunted animal — a deer or a bird killed out in the hills cannot be brought to the altar, so its blood is poured on the ground and buried. No priest, no altar, nobody watching. The rule reaches the one situation where there is no institution to enforce it, and makes it a matter of what a man does alone on a hillside with a spade.

chapters.title: Do Not Uncover
chapters.html:
Leviticus 18

Not Like Egypt, Not Like Canaan

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: I am the LORD your God.

3You shall not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived; and you shall not do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you; and you shall not walk in their statutes.

4You shall carry out My rulings and keep My statutes, and walk in them. I am the LORD your God.

5You shall keep My statutes and My rulings; the person who does them shall live by them. I am the LORD.

Whose Nakedness Is Not to Be Uncovered

6No man shall come near to anyone of his own flesh to uncover nakedness. I am the LORD.

7You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father, or the nakedness of your mother. She is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.

8You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife. It is your father's nakedness.

9You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, born at home or born outside.

10You shall not uncover the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, because their nakedness is your own.

11You shall not uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father. She is your sister.

12You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister. She is your father's flesh.

13You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, because she is your mother's flesh.

14You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's brother — you shall not come near his wife. She is your aunt.

15You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law. She is your son's wife; you shall not uncover her nakedness.

16You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife. It is your brother's nakedness.

17You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You shall not take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to uncover her nakedness. They are her own flesh. It is depravity.

18You shall not take a woman together with her sister, as a rival, to uncover her nakedness while she is alive.

And These

19You shall not come near a woman in the uncleanness of her monthly separation, to uncover her nakedness.

20You shall not lie with your neighbor's wife and so become unclean by her.

21You shall not give any of your children to pass over to Molech; and you shall not profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.

22You shall not lie with a male as one lies with a woman. It is detestable.

23You shall not lie with any animal and so become unclean by it; and a woman shall not stand in front of an animal to mate with it. It is a mixing.

What the Land Does

24Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these, because by all of these the nations I am driving out before you have made themselves unclean.

25The land became unclean, and I punished it for its guilt, and the land vomited out those living in it.

26But you shall keep My statutes and My rulings, and shall not do any of these detestable things — neither the native nor the guest living among you —

27because the people of the land who were before you did all these detestable things, and the land became unclean.

28Otherwise, when you make the land unclean, it will vomit you out as it vomited out the nation that was before you.

29For whoever does any of these detestable things — those who do them shall be cut off from among their people.

30You shall keep My charge, not to do any of the detestable statutes that were done before you, and not to make yourselves unclean by them. I am the LORD your God."

Notes

  • v5 "and live by them" — va-chai bahem, two words that became one of the most argued sentences in the Bible: the statutes are given so that a person may live by them. Ezekiel 20 quotes the exact phrase three times in one chapter (vv11, 13, 21) and then, at v25, says God gave them statutes that were not good and rules by which they could not live. The Hebrew here says only what it says, and does not define the living.

  • v6 "uncover nakedness" — gallot ervah, and the phrase runs through the chapter twenty-four times. Ervah is exposure, the state of being uncovered, and the idiom is a euphemism for sexual relations — Hebrew names the act by naming the shame of being seen. The chapter is built out of one sentence said over and over with the relative changed, which is why it reads like a list rather than an argument.

  • v18 "a woman together with her sister" — ishah el achotah, and this is the hardest verse in the chapter to be sure of. The phrase occurs in seven other places in the Hebrew Bible and in every one of them it is a fixed idiom meaning one to another, used of things: the curtains of the tabernacle coupled one to another (Exodus 26:3, 5, 6), the frames (26:17), the wings of the living creatures touching one another (Ezekiel 1:9, 23; 3:13). Not one of them is about a woman. So this verse can be read as forbidding marriage to a wife's sister — which is what Jacob did, and the word litsror, as a rival, points that way — or as forbidding taking one woman in addition to another at all. The two readings produce two different laws, and the Hebrew supports both.

  • v22 "as one lies with a woman" — mishkevei ishah, and the noun is plural: the lyings of a woman. The same plural appears in the parallel at 20:13 and nowhere else in the Bible, and what the plural is doing has never been settled. The verse ends with to'evah, the word Genesis uses for Egyptians eating with Hebrews (43:32) and for shepherds (46:34) — a term for what a given community will not have among it, which is a different kind of word from tamei, unclean, and from sheqets, loathsome, which chapter 11 used of animals.

  • vv25, 28 "the land vomited out" — va-taqi ha-arets, from qi, to vomit, and it is a physical verb used of a sick body. This is one of the few places in the Torah where the land is the one who acts (see also Exodus 15:12, Numbers 16:32). Not God expelling the Canaanites, not Israel conquering them: the ground itself is made nauseous and throws off what is on it. And v28 turns it on the audience — it will vomit you out as it vomited out the nation that was before you — which means the new occupants are being told they are on probation with the same soil.

chapters.title: Love Your Neighbor as Yourself
chapters.html:
Leviticus 19

You Shall Be Holy

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, because I, the LORD your God, am holy.

3Each of you shall fear his mother and his father, and you shall keep My sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.

4Do not turn to worthless gods, and do not make cast gods for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.

5When you sacrifice a peace offering to the LORD, you shall sacrifice it so that it is accepted for you.

6It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it and on the next day, and what is left until the third day shall be burned in the fire.

7If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is foul. It will not be accepted.

8Whoever eats it carries his guilt, because he has profaned what is holy to the LORD, and that person shall be cut off from his people.

What You Leave in the Field

9When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish reaping to the edge of your field, and you shall not gather the gleanings of your harvest.

10You shall not strip your vineyard bare, and you shall not gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard. You shall leave them for the poor and for the guest. I am the LORD your God.

How to Treat Each Other

11You shall not steal, and you shall not deal falsely, and you shall not lie to one another.

12You shall not swear falsely by My name, and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.

13You shall not exploit your neighbor and you shall not rob him. The wages of a hired man shall not stay with you overnight until morning.

14You shall not curse a deaf man, and you shall not put a stumbling block in front of a blind man; and you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.

15You shall not do injustice in judgment. You shall not show favor to the poor or defer to the great. In righteousness you shall judge your neighbor.

16You shall not go around spreading slander among your people. You shall not stand on the blood of your neighbor. I am the LORD.

17You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You shall be sure to correct your neighbor, and not carry guilt because of him.

18You shall not take revenge and you shall not hold a grudge against the sons of your people; and you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.

Mixtures

19You shall keep My statutes. You shall not mate your livestock with a different kind. You shall not sow your field with two kinds of seed. You shall not put on a garment woven of two kinds of material.

20When a man lies with a woman who is a slave promised to another man, and she has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there shall be an inquiry. They shall not be put to death, because she was not free.

21He shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting — a ram for a guilt offering.

22The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD, for the sin he has committed; and he shall be forgiven for it.

23When you enter the land and plant any tree for food, you shall treat its fruit as forbidden. For three years it shall be forbidden to you. It shall not be eaten.

24In the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, a praise offering to the LORD.

25In the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that it will yield more for you. I am the LORD your God.

Marks on the Body

26You shall not eat anything with the blood in it. You shall not practice divination and you shall not read omens.

27You shall not round off the hair at the sides of your head, and you shall not ruin the edge of your beard.

28You shall not make a gash in your flesh for the dead, and you shall not put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.

29Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will turn to prostitution and be filled with depravity.

30You shall keep My sabbaths and fear My sanctuary. I am the LORD.

31Do not turn to ghosts, and do not seek out spirits, and so become unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.

The Old, the Foreigner, the Scales

32You shall rise in the presence of the gray-haired and honor the old; and you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.

33When a guest lives with you in your land, you shall not wrong him.

34The guest living with you shall be to you as a native among you, and you shall love him as yourself, because you were guests in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.

35You shall not do injustice in judgment — in measuring length, in weight, or in quantity.

36You shall have honest scales, honest weights, an honest ephah and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.

37You shall keep all My statutes and all My rulings and do them. I am the LORD."

Notes

  • vv9–10 what is left in the field — four things: the edge of the field is not reaped, the dropped stalks are not picked up, the vineyard is not stripped, the fallen grapes are not gathered. The poor and the guest are not given anything — they are left something, and they come and take it themselves. This is the law Ruth is working under in Boaz's field, and it is written as a restriction on the owner rather than as a charity.

  • v16 "stand on the blood of your neighbor" — lo ta'amod al dam re'ekha, and what it means is not clear. The preposition can be on, against, beside or over; the phrase might forbid profiting from a neighbor's death, standing by while his life is at risk, or testifying in a capital case. The first half of the verse is about carrying tales, which suggests speech. The Hebrew supports more than one reading and nothing in the verse settles it.

  • vv18 and 34 the sentence and its twin — ve-ahavta le-re'akha kamokha, and you shall love your neighbor as yourself, is the most quoted line in Leviticus. Sixteen verses later the identical construction is used again, of somebody else: ve-ahavta lo kamokha, and you shall love him as yourself, said of the ger, the guest living in your land. Those two verses are the only places in the entire Hebrew Bible where this phrase occurs. The famous one has a twin, and the twin is almost never quoted.

  • v20 the hardest verse in the chapter — two of its words are effectively unrecoverable. Necherefet, describing the woman's status, occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, in this verse; it is usually taken as designated or promised to a man. Biqqoret, the consequence, also occurs once in this form, and has been read as an inquiry, a distinction in punishment, and compensation. What the verse plainly says is that the two are not put to death, and that the reason is her legal condition: because she was not free.

  • v23 "you shall treat its fruit as forbidden" — the Hebrew is va-araltem orlato, you shall foreskin its foreskin, the verb taking its own noun, and the noun is the word for the foreskin removed at circumcision. Young fruit is spoken of as uncircumcised, so the tree is under the same language as a child in its first days.

  • v28 "tattoo marks" — ketovet qa'aqa, and qa'aqa occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, in this verse. It sits beside a ban on gashing the flesh la-nefesh, for the dead — both are mourning practices, cut into the body. The two halves of the verse belong together, and the ban is not on marking as such but on marking oneself over a death.

You shall not eat anything with the blood in it. You shall not practice divination and you shall not read omens.

Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will turn to prostitution and be filled with depravity.
You shall keep My sabbaths and fear My sanctuary. I am the LORD.
Do not turn to ghosts, and do not seek out spirits, and so become unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.

You shall rise in the presence of the gray-haired and honor the old; and you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.
When a guest lives with you in your land, you shall not wrong him.
The guest living with you shall be to you as a native among you, and you shall love him as yourself, because you were guests in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
You shall not do injustice in judgment — in measuring length, in weight, or in quantity.
You shall have honest scales, honest weights, an honest ephah and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
You shall keep all My statutes and all My rulings and do them. I am the LORD."

chapters.title: What It Costs
chapters.html:
Leviticus 20

Molech, and the Ones Who Look Away

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Say to the sons of Israel: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the guests living in Israel, who gives any of his children to Molech shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him.

3I Myself will set My face against that man, and cut him off from among his people, because he gave of his children to Molech, and so made My sanctuary unclean and profaned My holy name.

4If the people of the land deliberately shut their eyes to that man when he gives his children to Molech, and do not put him to death,

5then I Myself will set My face against that man and against his family, and cut him off from among their people — him and all who follow him in giving themselves to Molech.

6The person who turns to ghosts and to spirits, giving themselves to them — I will set My face against that person and cut him off from among his people.

7You shall set yourselves apart and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.

8You shall keep My statutes and do them. I am the LORD who makes you holy.

The Penalties

9Any man who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death. He has cursed his father and his mother; his blood is on his own head.

10A man who commits adultery with another man's wife — who commits adultery with his neighbor's wife — the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.

11A man who lies with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness. Both of them shall surely be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.

12A man who lies with his daughter-in-law — both of them shall surely be put to death. They have done a mixing; their blood is on their own heads.

13A man who lies with a male as one lies with a woman — both of them have done a detestable thing. They shall surely be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.

14A man who takes a woman and her mother — it is depravity. They shall burn him and them in the fire, so that there shall be no depravity among you.

15A man who lies with an animal shall surely be put to death, and you shall kill the animal.

16A woman who comes near any animal to mate with it — you shall kill the woman and the animal. They shall surely be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.

17A man who takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness — it is a disgrace. They shall be cut off in the sight of their people. He has uncovered his sister's nakedness; he carries his guilt.

18A man who lies with a woman in her sickness and uncovers her nakedness — he has laid bare her source, and she has uncovered the source of her blood. Both of them shall be cut off from among their people.

19You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister or of your father's sister, because that lays bare his own flesh. They shall carry their guilt.

20A man who lies with his uncle's wife has uncovered his uncle's nakedness. They shall carry their sin; they shall die childless.

21A man who takes his brother's wife — it is an impurity. He has uncovered his brother's nakedness. They shall be childless.

Why You Are Not Like Them

22You shall keep all My statutes and all My rulings and do them, so that the land I am bringing you into to live in does not vomit you out.

23You shall not walk in the statutes of the nation I am driving out before you, because they did all these things, and I was sick of them.

24I said to you: You shall take possession of their ground, and I will give it to you as your own — a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.

25You shall separate the clean animal from the unclean, and the unclean bird from the clean, and you shall not make yourselves loathsome with any animal or bird or anything that creeps on the ground, which I have separated out for you as unclean.

26You shall be holy to Me, because I the LORD am holy, and I have separated you from the peoples to be Mine.

27A man or a woman who has a ghost or a spirit in them shall surely be put to death. They shall stone them; their blood is on their own heads."

Notes

  • v17 "it is a disgrace" — the Hebrew word is chesed, and this is one of the strangest sentences in the Bible. Chesed is the great covenant word: loyal love, steadfast kindness, the thing God is said to keep for a thousand generations, the word in I desire mercy and not sacrifice (Hosea 6:6) and all through the Psalms. Here it names an act punished by being cut off. The spelling is identical and so is the vowel pointing — this is not a look-alike. Either one root carried two opposite senses, shame and devotion, or a second root has been swallowed by the first. Nothing in the verse decides it.

  • vv24–26 "separated" — badal four times in three verses, and it is the verb of Genesis 1, where God separates light from darkness and waters from waters. The chapter's closing argument is built out of it: I separated you from the peoples (v24), so you separate clean animals from unclean (v25), from things I separated out for you (v25), because I separated you to be Mine (v26). The dietary law and the election of Israel are stated as one act, in one word, four times over. It is the same verb handed to the priesthood at 10:10 and used to close chapter 11.

chapters.title: Rules for the Priests
chapters.html:
Leviticus 21

A Priest and the Dead

1The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: None of them shall make himself unclean for a dead person among his people,

2except for his own flesh closest to him — for his mother and for his father, and for his son and for his daughter and for his brother,

3and for his unmarried sister, who is close to him because she has had no husband. For her he may make himself unclean.

4He shall not make himself unclean as a husband among his people, profaning himself.

5They shall not make a bald patch on their heads, and they shall not shave off the edge of their beards, and they shall not cut a gash in their flesh.

6They shall be holy to their God, and they shall not profane the name of their God, because they present the LORD's offerings by fire, the bread of their God. They shall be holy.

7They shall not take a woman who is a prostitute or who has been disgraced, and they shall not take a woman divorced from her husband, because he is holy to his God.

8You shall treat him as holy, because he presents the bread of your God. He shall be holy to you, because I the LORD, who makes you holy, am holy.

9A priest's daughter, if she profanes herself by whoring, profanes her father. She shall be burned in the fire.

The High Priest

10The priest who is greatest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil was poured and whose hand was filled to wear the garments, shall not let his hair hang loose and shall not tear his clothes.

11He shall not go near any dead body. He shall not make himself unclean even for his father or for his mother.

12He shall not go out of the sanctuary and profane the sanctuary of his God, because the crown of the anointing oil of his God is on him. I am the LORD.

13He shall take as his wife a woman who is a virgin.

14A widow, or a divorced woman, or a woman disgraced by prostitution — these he shall not take. He shall take a virgin from his own people as a wife,

15and he shall not profane his offspring among his people, because I am the LORD who makes him holy."

A Blemish

16The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

17"Speak to Aaron, saying: None of your offspring through their generations who has a blemish shall come near to present the bread of his God.

18No man at all who has a blemish shall come near: a man who is blind or lame, or disfigured in the face, or with a limb too long,

19or a man who has a broken foot or a broken hand,

20or a hunchback, or a withered man, or one with a spot in his eye, or a scab, or a skin eruption, or crushed testicles.

21No man of the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a blemish shall come forward to present the LORD's offerings by fire. He has a blemish; he shall not come forward to present the bread of his God.

22He may eat the bread of his God, both the most holy and the holy.

23But he shall not come to the veil and shall not come near the altar, because he has a blemish, and he shall not profane My holy places, because I am the LORD who makes them holy."

24Moses spoke this to Aaron and to his sons and to all the sons of Israel.

Notes

  • v4 the broken verse — lo yittamma ba'al be-ammav le-hechallo, and it is one of the least recoverable sentences in Leviticus. Ba'al means a husband, an owner, a master; be-ammav is among his people; le-hechallo is to profane himself. The words are all ordinary and the sentence they make is not. It has been read as a rule about a priest's wife, about a chief among his kin, and as the conclusion of vv1–3.

  • vv18–20 the list nobody can fully translate — twelve conditions, and several of the words are effectively unknown. Tevallul occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, in v20. Sarua occurs twice, both in Leviticus, and is usually taken as a limb of the wrong length. Charum is guessed from a root for cutting, so a damaged face. The English in every Bible is a reconstruction from roots and from the company the words keep, and the confident-sounding lists in modern translations are covering a good deal of uncertainty.

chapters.title: Who May Eat the Holy Things
chapters.html:
Leviticus 22

The Priests and the Holy Things

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to Aaron and to his sons, that they keep themselves apart from the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they set apart for Me, and not profane My holy name. I am the LORD.

3Say to them: Throughout your generations, any man of all your offspring who comes near to the holy things that the sons of Israel set apart for the LORD while he is unclean — that person shall be cut off from My presence. I am the LORD.

4No man at all of the offspring of Aaron who has blight or a discharge shall eat of the holy things until he is clean. Whoever touches anything made unclean by a dead person, or a man who has an emission of semen,

5or a man who touches any swarming thing that makes him unclean, or any person who makes him unclean, whatever his uncleanness —

6the person who touches any of these shall be unclean until evening, and shall not eat of the holy things unless he has washed his body in water.

7When the sun goes down he will be clean, and afterward he may eat of the holy things, because it is his bread.

8He shall not eat an animal that died on its own or was torn by beasts, and so make himself unclean by it. I am the LORD.

9They shall keep My charge, so that they do not carry sin because of it and die for profaning it. I am the LORD who makes them holy.

10No outsider shall eat a holy thing. A priest's resident or a hired man shall not eat a holy thing.

11But if a priest buys a person with his money, that person may eat of it, and so may those born in his house; they may eat of his bread.

12A priest's daughter who is married to an outsider shall not eat of the holy contributions.

13But a priest's daughter who is widowed or divorced, and has no child, and has come back to her father's house as in her youth, may eat of her father's bread. But no outsider shall eat of it.

14If a man eats a holy thing by mistake, he shall add a fifth to it and give the holy thing back to the priest.

15They shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they raise up to the LORD,

16and so make them carry guilt that must be paid for, by eating their holy things. For I am the LORD who makes them holy."

An Offering Must Be Whole

17The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

18"Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all the sons of Israel, and say to them: Any man at all of the house of Israel, or of the guests living in Israel, who brings his offering for any of their vows or any of their freewill offerings, which they bring to the LORD as a burnt offering —

19to be accepted for you, it must be a male without defect, from the cattle, from the sheep, or from the goats.

20Anything that has a blemish you shall not bring, because it will not be accepted for you.

21If a man brings a sacrifice of peace offering to the LORD to fulfill a special vow, or as a freewill offering, from the herd or from the flock, it must be without defect to be accepted. There shall be no blemish in it.

22Blind, or broken, or maimed, or with a wart, or a scab, or a skin eruption — you shall not bring these to the LORD, and you shall not put an offering by fire from them on the altar to the LORD.

23You may offer as a freewill offering an ox or a sheep with a limb too long or too short, but it will not be accepted for a vow.

24You shall not offer to the LORD an animal whose testicles are bruised, or crushed, or torn, or cut, and in your land you shall not do this.

25You shall not take any of these from a foreigner and offer them as the bread of your God, because their ruin is in them; there is a blemish in them. They will not be accepted for you."

The Eighth Day

26The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

27"When an ox or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall stay seven days with its mother, and from the eighth day on it will be accepted as an offering by fire to the LORD.

28Whether ox or sheep, you shall not slaughter it and its young on the same day.

29When you offer a thanksgiving sacrifice to the LORD, offer it so that it is accepted for you.

30It shall be eaten on that same day; you shall leave none of it until morning. I am the LORD.

31You shall keep My commandments and do them. I am the LORD.

32You shall not profane My holy name, and I will be shown holy among the sons of Israel. I am the LORD who makes you holy,

33who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD."

Notes

  • v22 "with a wart" — yabbelet occurs here and nowhere else in the Hebrew Bible. The Greek has myrmēkiōnta, warted; the other old reading is a running sore, and with one occurrence in a list, nothing in the Hebrew settles it. Scab and skin eruption are the two words of 21:20: the same faults that keep a priest from the altar keep an animal off it.

  • v24 "in your land you shall not do this" — the Hebrew does not say what this is. It can mean do not offer such animals, which repeats the first half of the verse, or do not do this to animals at all, which would forbid gelding. Both readings are old, and the words allow either.

  • v32 "I will be shown holy" — ve-niqdashti, the same verb Moses quoted at the death of Nadab and Abihu: through those near Me I will be shown holy (10:3, eqqadesh). The chapter turns on one pair of words: profane, chillel, four times (vv2, 9, 15, 32), against holy. God's name is either profaned or shown holy by how Israel handles what belongs to Him.

chapters.title: The Appointed Times
chapters.html:
Leviticus 23

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: The appointed times of the LORD, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies — these are My appointed times.

The Sabbath

3Work may be done for six days, but on the seventh day is a sabbath of complete rest, a holy assembly. You shall do no work at all. It is a sabbath to the LORD in all your dwellings.

Passover and Unleavened Bread

4These are the appointed times of the LORD, holy assemblies, which you shall proclaim at their appointed time.

5In the first month, on the fourteenth of the month, between the evenings, is the LORD's Passover.

6On the fifteenth day of this month is the Festival of Unleavened Bread to the LORD. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.

7On the first day you shall have a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.

8You shall present an offering by fire to the LORD for seven days. On the seventh day is a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work."

The First Sheaf

9The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

10"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you enter the land that I am giving you, and you reap its harvest, you shall bring the first sheaf of your harvest to the priest.

11He shall wave the sheaf before the LORD, so that it is accepted for you. On the day after the sabbath the priest shall wave it.

12On the day you wave the sheaf you shall offer a lamb a year old without defect as a burnt offering to the LORD,

13and its grain offering, two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering by fire to the LORD, a soothing aroma; and its drink offering, wine, a fourth of a hin.

14You shall eat no bread, roasted grain or fresh grain until that very day, until you have brought the offering of your God. It is a lasting statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.

Fifty Days

15You shall count for yourselves from the day after the sabbath, from the day you bring the sheaf of the wave offering: there shall be seven full sabbaths.

16Until the day after the seventh sabbath you shall count fifty days, and you shall present a new grain offering to the LORD.

17From your dwellings you shall bring two loaves of bread for waving, made of two tenths of fine flour. They shall be baked with leaven, as firstfruits to the LORD.

18With the bread you shall present seven lambs a year old without defect, and one young bull, and two rams. They shall be a burnt offering to the LORD, with their grain offering and their drink offerings, an offering by fire, a soothing aroma to the LORD.

19You shall offer one male goat as a sin offering, and two lambs a year old as a sacrifice of peace offerings.

20The priest shall wave them before the LORD with the bread of the firstfruits, together with the two lambs. They shall be holy to the LORD, for the priest.

21On that very day you shall proclaim a holy assembly for yourselves. You shall do no ordinary work. It is a lasting statute in all your dwellings throughout your generations.

The First of the Seventh Month

23The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

24"Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: In the seventh month, on the first of the month, you shall have a rest, a remembrance with horn blasts, a holy assembly.

25You shall do no ordinary work, and you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD."

The Day of Atonement

26The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

27"But on the tenth of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. It shall be a holy assembly for you, and you shall afflict yourselves, and you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD.

28You shall do no work at all on that very day, because it is a Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.

29For any person who does not afflict himself on that very day shall be cut off from his people.

30Any person who does any work at all on that very day — I will destroy that person from among his people.

31You shall do no work at all. It is a lasting statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.

32It is a sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall afflict yourselves. On the ninth of the month at evening, from evening to evening, you shall keep your sabbath."

Booths

33The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

34"Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Festival of Booths, seven days to the LORD.

35On the first day is a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.

36For seven days you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day you shall have a holy assembly, and you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a closing assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.

37These are the appointed times of the LORD, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies, for presenting offerings by fire to the LORD — burnt offering and grain offering, sacrifice and drink offerings, each on its own day —

38besides the LORD's sabbaths, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vows, and besides all your freewill offerings, which you give to the LORD.

39But on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you shall keep the festival of the LORD seven days. On the first day is a rest, and on the eighth day is a rest.

40On the first day you shall take for yourselves the fruit of splendid trees, branches of palm trees, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the brook, and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God seven days.

41You shall keep it as a festival to the LORD seven days in the year. It is a lasting statute throughout your generations. In the seventh month you shall keep it.

42You shall live in booths for seven days. Every native Israelite shall live in booths,

43so that your generations may know that I made the sons of Israel live in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."

44Moses told the sons of Israel the appointed times of the LORD.

Notes

  • v2 "appointed times… holy assemblies" — mo'adim, from ya'ad, to fix a meeting: the word of the tent of meeting, ohel mo'ed, and of the lights in Genesis 1:14, set in the sky for appointed times. The calendar is a set of meetings with God, and the sun and moon were made to keep them. Holy assembly is miqra qodesh, from qara, to call: a holy calling. The verb in the same verse is which you shall call them, so the day is named for the summons that gathers the people.

  • v11 "on the day after the sabbath" — the text does not say which sabbath: the weekly Sabbath, or the first day of Unleavened Bread (v7), which is kept like one. The two readings put the sheaf, and the fifty days that are counted from it, on different dates.

  • vv15–16 "seven full sabbaths… fifty days" — sabbath here also means the week it closes. Seven weeks are counted, and the fiftieth day is the festival. The Greek word for fiftieth is pentēkostē, and it is the name the New Testament gives this day: when the day of Pentecost had come (Acts 2:1).

  • v24 "a remembrance with horn blasts" — zikhron teru'ah. Teru'ah is a blast or a great shout: it is the shout that brings down Jericho's walls (Joshua 6:5), and the shofar teru'ah, the horn blast, of the jubilee (25:9). This verse names no instrument, and it does not say what is remembered. The day is the first of the seventh month; nothing in the text calls it a new year.

  • v40 "you shall rejoice" — u-semachtem, and it is the first time in the Bible that God commands people to rejoice. Genesis and Exodus mention gladness; neither commands it. The command comes with the harvest in, living in booths.

  • vv42–43 "booths… when I brought them out" — sukkot. On the night they left Egypt, the first place Israel camped was a town called Sukkot, Booths (Exodus 12:37). The festival makes every generation live where the first night out of slavery was spent.

chapters.title: The Lamp, the Bread, and the Name
chapters.html:
Leviticus 24

The Lamp and the Bread

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Command the sons of Israel to bring you clear oil of beaten olives for the light, to set up a lamp continually.

3Outside the veil of the Testimony, in the tent of meeting, Aaron shall set it in order from evening until morning before the LORD continually. It is a lasting statute throughout your generations.

4On the pure lampstand he shall set the lamps in order before the LORD continually.

5You shall take fine flour and bake twelve loaves from it. Each loaf shall be two tenths.

6You shall set them in two rows, six to a row, on the pure table before the LORD.

7You shall put pure frankincense on each row, and it shall be a memorial portion for the bread, an offering by fire to the LORD.

8Every sabbath day he shall set it in order before the LORD continually. It is from the sons of Israel, an everlasting covenant.

9It shall be Aaron's and his sons', and they shall eat it in a holy place, because it is most holy to him, from the LORD's offerings by fire — a lasting due."

The Man Who Cursed

10The son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian man, went out among the sons of Israel. The son of the Israelite woman and an Israelite man fought in the camp.

11The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name, and cursed. They brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.

12They put him in custody until the LORD's decision should be made clear to them.

13The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

14"Take the one who cursed outside the camp, and let all who heard lay their hands on his head, and let all the congregation stone him.

15Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: Any man at all who curses his God shall carry his sin.

16Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall surely stone him. The guest as well as the native, when he blasphemes the Name, shall be put to death.

17A man who strikes down any human life shall surely be put to death.

18Whoever strikes down the life of an animal shall make it good, life for life.

19A man who puts a blemish on his neighbor — as he has done, so it shall be done to him:

20break for break, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As he has put a blemish on a person, so it shall be put on him.

21Whoever strikes down an animal shall make it good, and whoever strikes down a human shall be put to death.

22You shall have one law, for the guest and for the native alike, because I am the LORD your God."

23Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and they took the one who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him. The sons of Israel did as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Notes

  • v11 "blasphemed the Name" — va-yiqqov, from naqav. The verb means to pierce, and also to mark out by name: the men who were designated by name in Numbers 1:17. Balaam uses it for cursing: How can I put a curse on one God has not cursed? (Numbers 23:8). The Name, ha-shem, stands alone, without of the LORD, the first time in the Bible that God's name is called simply the Name. Verse 16 then gives it in full.

chapters.title: The Sabbath Year and the Jubilee
chapters.html:
Leviticus 25

A Sabbath for the Land

1The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,

2"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you enter the land that I am giving you, the land shall keep a sabbath to the LORD.

3For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather in its produce.

4But in the seventh year there shall be a sabbath of complete rest for the land, a sabbath to the LORD. You shall not sow your field or prune your vineyard.

5You shall not reap what grows by itself from your harvest, or gather the grapes of your untrimmed vine. It shall be a year of complete rest for the land.

6The sabbath of the land shall be food for you — for you, and for your male slave and your female slave, and for your hired man and your resident, who live with you as guests,

7and for your livestock and for the wild animals that are in your land. All its produce shall be food.

The Jubilee

8You shall count for yourself seven sabbaths of years, seven years seven times, so that the days of the seven sabbaths of years come to forty-nine years.

9Then you shall send the horn's blast through the land, in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month. On the Day of Atonement you shall send the horn through all your land.

10You shall make the fiftieth year holy, and proclaim liberty in the land to all who live in it. It shall be a jubilee for you, and each of you shall return to his holding and to his family.

11That fiftieth year shall be a jubilee for you. You shall not sow, and you shall not reap what grows by itself, and you shall not gather the grapes of its untrimmed vines.

12Because it is a jubilee, it shall be holy to you. You shall eat its produce straight from the field.

13In this year of jubilee you shall return, each man to his holding.

14If you sell something to your neighbor, or buy from your neighbor, you shall not wrong one another.

15By the number of years since the jubilee you shall buy from your neighbor; by the number of years of harvests he shall sell to you.

16The more the years, the higher you shall make its price; the fewer the years, the lower you shall make its price, because it is a number of harvests that he is selling you.

17You shall not wrong one another, but you shall fear your God, because I am the LORD your God.

18You shall do My statutes, and keep My rulings and do them, and you will live in the land in security.

19The land will give its fruit, and you will eat your fill and live in it in security.

20If you say, 'What shall we eat in the seventh year, if we may not sow or gather in our produce?' —

21I will command My blessing for you in the sixth year, and it will produce enough for three years.

22You will sow in the eighth year and eat of the old produce until the ninth year. Until its produce comes in, you will eat the old.

Redeeming the Land

23The land shall not be sold for good, because the land is Mine. For you are guests and residents with Me.

24In all the land you hold, you shall allow the land to be redeemed.

25If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his holding, his redeemer who is closest to him shall come and redeem what his brother has sold.

26If a man has no one to redeem it, and he himself prospers and finds enough to redeem it,

27he shall count the years since he sold it, and pay back what remains to the man he sold it to, and return to his holding.

28But if he has not found enough to pay him back, then what he sold shall remain in the hand of the one who bought it until the year of jubilee. It shall go out in the jubilee, and he shall return to his holding.

29If a man sells a house to live in, in a walled city, his right to redeem it shall last until a full year after its sale. For a year he may redeem it.

30If it is not redeemed before a full year has passed, the house in the walled city shall belong for good to the one who bought it, throughout his generations. It shall not go out in the jubilee.

31But the houses of villages that have no wall around them shall be counted as the fields of the land. They may be redeemed, and they shall go out in the jubilee.

32As for the cities of the Levites, the houses in the cities they hold — the Levites shall always have the right to redeem them.

33If one of the Levites redeems it, then the house that was sold in the city he holds shall go out in the jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their holding among the sons of Israel.

34The pasture land around their cities shall not be sold, because it is their holding forever.

A Brother Who Becomes Poor

35If your brother becomes poor and his hand fails beside you, you shall hold him up. As a guest and a resident, he shall live with you.

36Take no interest from him and no increase, but fear your God, so that your brother may live with you.

37You shall not give him your money at interest, and you shall not give him your food for increase.

38I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan, to be your God.

39If your brother becomes poor beside you and sells himself to you, you shall not make him work as a slave works.

40As a hired man, as a resident, he shall be with you. Until the year of jubilee he shall work with you.

41Then he shall go out from you, he and his sons with him, and he shall return to his family and to the holding of his fathers.

42For they are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They shall not be sold as a slave is sold.

43You shall not rule over him with crushing harshness, but you shall fear your God.

44The male and female slaves you may have are to come from the nations around you; from them you may buy male and female slaves.

45Also from the sons of the residents who live with you as guests, from them you may buy, and from their families that are with you, whom they have fathered in your land. They may be your property.

46You may leave them to your sons after you, to inherit as property. You may make them work for you forever. But over your brothers, the sons of Israel, one over another, you shall not rule with crushing harshness.

47If a guest or a resident with you prospers, and your brother beside him becomes poor and sells himself to the guest or resident with you, or to an offshoot of the guest's family,

48after he is sold he shall have the right to be redeemed. One of his brothers may redeem him,

49or his uncle or his uncle's son may redeem him, or anyone of his own flesh from his family may redeem him, or if he prospers he may redeem himself.

50He shall reckon with the one who bought him from the year he sold himself to him until the year of jubilee, and the price of his sale shall be according to the number of years. His time with him shall be counted like the days of a hired man.

51If many years remain, he shall pay back for his redemption a matching part of the price he was bought for.

52If few years remain until the year of jubilee, he shall reckon it with him; according to his years he shall pay back his redemption.

53He shall be with the buyer like a man hired year by year, and the buyer shall not rule over him with crushing harshness in your sight.

54If he is not redeemed by these means, then he shall go out in the year of jubilee, he and his sons with him.

55For the sons of Israel are servants to Me. They are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."

Notes

  • v10 "proclaim liberty… a jubilee" — deror, release, the freeing of those held. Isaiah takes up the phrase for the one anointed to proclaim liberty to the captives (61:1), and Jesus reads that line aloud in the synagogue at Nazareth (Luke 4:18). The Liberty Bell in Philadelphia carries this verse. Jubilee is yovel, the ram, and so the ram's horn: the horns blown at Jericho are yovel horns (Joshua 6:5). The year is named for the sound that starts it.

  • v23 "for you are guests and residents with Me" — gerim ve-toshavim, the same two words Abraham used of himself to the Hittites when he had no land to bury Sarah in: a guest and a resident I am among you (Genesis 23:4). Israel is to hold the land the way Abraham lived in it: as a guest of the owner, who is God.

  • v25 "his redeemer" — go'alo, from ga'al, to buy back what belongs to the family. The go'el is the nearest relative, whose duty is to redeem the land, or the man, before they are lost. Boaz is the go'el who redeems Naomi's field and marries Ruth (Ruth 4:4), and Job says I know that my redeemer lives (Job 19:25). It is the same word.

  • v30 "the house in the walled city" — the Hebrew text as written says the city which has not a wall, lo, spelled with an aleph. The reading marked in the margin is lo spelled with a vav, which has a wall, and v29 shows that is the sense. It is one of five places in Leviticus where the written word and the read word differ.

  • vv42, 55 "My servants" — avadai. Hebrew has one word, eved, for both servant and slave: it is the slave sold in the same sentence and the slaves of Egypt. Israel belongs to God, and so may be sold to no human master. At the sea the people said it would be better to serve Egypt (Exodus 14:12). The law answers that they already serve someone else.
